## Background {auto-animate="true"}


<div class="approach-lead">How to define &ldquo;good&rdquo; LLM feedback</div>

<div class="approach-row">

<div class="approach fragment">
  <span class="num">1</span>
  <span class="approach-title">Align with faculty</span>
  <span class="approach-note">Prompt and rate LLMs for feedback that closely matches what faculty wrote.</span>
  <span class="cite">(Shakur et al., 2024; R&uuml;dian et al., 2025)</span>
</div>

<div class="approach chosen fragment">
  <span class="tag">Our research</span>
  <span class="num">2</span>
  <span class="approach-title">Align with pedagogy</span>
  <span class="approach-note">Prompt and rate LLMs for feedback that aligns with best assessment practices and feedback science. Rate faculty feedback independently.</span>
  <span class="cite">(Dai et al., 2024; Hattie &amp; Timperley, 2007; K&#x131;yak et al., 2026)</span>
</div>

</div>

## OSCE Rubric {auto-animate="true"}


<div class="approach-lead">How to assess students</div>

<div class="approach-row">

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="num wide">38</span>
<span class="approach-title">Checkboxes</span>
<span class="approach-note">Done or Not Done, from <span class="hl">washing hands</span> to <span class="hl">listening to both lungs</span> to the <span class="hl">teach-back</span>. They average into a score and decile.</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="num wide">4</span>
<span class="approach-title">Global ratings</span>
<span class="approach-note"><span class="hl">History</span>, <span class="hl">physical exam</span>, <span class="hl">clinical reasoning</span>, and <span class="hl">communication</span> &mdash; each judged against expectations for this level of training.</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="num wide">1</span>
<span class="approach-title">Paragraph of formative feedback</span>
<span class="approach-note">A short <span class="hl">written comment </span>about the student's performance.</span>
</div>

</div>

## Quality of Feedback Rubric {auto-animate="true"}


<div class="approach-lead">How to assess feedback</div>

<div class="quad">

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="approach-title">Specific</span>
<span class="approach-note">Names the behavior and the <span class="hl">gap</span> between current and expected performance</span>
<span class="cite">(Hattie &amp; Timperley, 2007; Wisniewski et al., 2020)</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="approach-title">Constructive</span>
<span class="approach-note">Gives the student something <span class="hl">actionable</span> to do next time</span>
<span class="cite">(Hattie &amp; Timperley, 2007; Lefroy et al., 2015)</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="approach-title">Balanced</span>
<span class="approach-note">Covers <span class="hl">strengths and gaps</span>, not only what went wrong</span>
<span class="cite">(Lefroy et al., 2015)</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="approach-title">Behavioral</span>
<span class="approach-note">Describes <span class="hl">observed actions</span>, not personal attributes</span>
<span class="cite">(Ende, 1983; Alsahafi et al., 2023)</span>
</div>

<div class="approach gate fragment">
<span class="approach-title">Accurate</span>
<span class="approach-note">LLM feedback shows <span class="hl">variable accuracy</span>. A confident wrong claim can <span class="hl">harm learning or care</span>.</span>
<span class="cite">(K&#x131;yak et al., 2026)</span>
</div>

</div>

## Rating Design {auto-animate="true"}

<div class="approach-lead">How the feedback was rated</div>

<div class="foot-note">Pilot to test the workflow and the instrument before scaling to 130 transcripts</div>

<div class="approach-row">

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="num wide">5</span>
<span class="approach-title">Blinded raters</span>
<span class="approach-note">Faculty/staff rate each comment <span class="hl">without knowing</span> whether an LLM or a colleague wrote it.</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="num wide">4</span>
<span class="approach-title">Conditions</span>
<span class="approach-note">The three prompt versions &mdash; <span class="hl">V0</span>, <span class="hl">V1</span>, <span class="hl">V2</span> &mdash; and <span class="hl">faculty feedback</span>.</span>
</div>

<div class="approach fragment">
<span class="num wide">25</span>
<span class="approach-title">Pilot ratings</span>
<span class="approach-note"><span class="hl">5 transcripts</span> stratified across deciles &times; <span class="hl">5 raters</span>.</span>
</div>

</div>

::: {.matrix .fragment}
| Transcript | Rater 1 | Rater 2 | Rater 3 | Rater 4 | Rater 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | V0 | V1 | V2 | FF | V2 |
| T2 | V1 | V2 | FF | V0 | V0 |
| T3 | V2 | FF | V0 | V1 | V2 |
| T4 | FF | V0 | V1 | V2 | V1 |
| T5 | V1 | V0 | V2 | FF | V1 |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20,16,16,16,16,16]"}

[Counterbalanced across raters, so one condition repeats per transcript. FF = faculty feedback.]{.cite}
:::
